item.title: Cuba publishes names of 2,000 pardoned prisoners
item.description: Cuba on Monday disclosed the identities of more than 2,000 prisoners pardoned under a sweeping amnesty first announced in April, publishing their names in the country's official government gazette for the first time since the decree was signed nearly two months ago.

item.title: Zelensky says US missile defense talks have stalled
item.description: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Monday that strengthening Ukraine's air defense is Kyiv's "first priority" and disclosed that talks with the United States on expanding anti-ballistic missile production have stalled, pushing Ukraine to accelerate its own efforts in Europe.

item.title: Iran warns of strikes 'beyond regional borders' after US hits southern Iran
item.description: Iran's armed forces issued sharp warnings on Tuesday, May 26, threatening an expanded and more devastating military response if the United States and Israel resume strikes, after Washington carried out what it described as "self-defense strikes" in southern Iran near the Strait of Hormuz over the preceding 48 hours.

item.title: BP removes chairman Albert Manifold over conduct concerns
item.description: BP on Tuesday removed Albert Manifold as chairman and director with immediate effect, citing "serious concerns" related to governance standards, oversight, and conduct — a sudden ouster that came just eight months into his tenure atop the British oil giant.

item.title: Iran's judiciary blocks presidential order to restore internet
item.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian ordered the restoration of international internet access on May 25, seeking to end what has become the longest nationwide internet shutdown in history. Internet monitoring group NetBlocks confirmed partial connectivity was restored on Tuesday. But within hours, Iran's judiciary suspended the very presidential body responsible for carrying out the order, plunging the country's digital future into uncertainty.

item.title: Israel intensifies Lebanon strikes as US-Iran deal nears
item.description: Israel is pressing the United States to guarantee its continued freedom to conduct military operations in Lebanon as part of any emerging peace framework with Iran, even as Israeli airstrikes killed multiple people in Lebanon's Bekaa Valley on Tuesday and the country's opposition leader declared the prospective agreement a failure.

item.title: Iran calls U.S. strikes a ceasefire breach as Qatar talks continue
item.description: The U.S. military launched strikes against missile installations and vessels in southern Iran on Monday, targeting sites near Bandar Abbas along the Strait of Hormuz, in a move that drew immediate condemnation from Tehran and threatened to upend fragile peace negotiations taking place simultaneously in Qatar.

item.title: UN Security Council condemns drone strike on UAE nuclear plant
item.description: The United Nations Security Council on Tuesday unanimously condemned the drone attack on the Barakah Nuclear Power Plant in the United Arab Emirates, calling it a violation of international law, according to Reuters. The statement came more than a week after a drone struck an electrical generator at the Arab world's only nuclear power facility on May 17, sparking a fire but causing no injuries or radiation release.

item.title: UK and Poland to sign defense treaty targeting Russian threats
item.description: Prime Minister Keir Starmer and Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk are set to sign a defence and security treaty in London on Wednesday, marking the latest in a series of bilateral agreements Britain has struck with European partners to confront what officials describe as escalating hostile threats across the continent.

item.title: Cuba calls US oil blockade 'an act of war' at UN Security Council
item.description:
Cuba's Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla addressed the United Nations Security Council on Tuesday, warning that the U.S. oil blockade against his country amounts to an act of war and calling on the international community to mobilize against what he described as an unfolding humanitarian catastrophe.

"The oil and energy siege imposed by the United States against Cuba is, in its effects, equivalent to a naval blockade — an act of war," Rodríguez said, according to a statement posted by Cuba's foreign ministry. He added that "the government of the United States, by its deeds, is in a position to erode international peace and security."

"I call on the international community to mobilize to prevent a humanitarian catastrophe that could be imposed through arms or the fuel blockade," he told the council, adding that "now should be the time for solidarity with Cuba."

item.title: North Korea claims first use of AI in missile tests
item.description: North Korea on Wednesday announced it had tested a range of advanced weapons systems, including cruise missiles guided by artificial intelligence, marking the first time Pyongyang has publicly claimed to incorporate AI into its missile technology. Leader Kim Jong Un supervised the tests on Tuesday, state media KCNA reported.

item.title: Iran state TV says it obtained draft MOU framework with US
item.description: Iran's state television reported on Wednesday that it had obtained a draft of an initial unofficial framework for a Memorandum of Understanding with the United States, according to Reuters. The development marks the latest step in weeks of intensive diplomacy aimed at ending the conflict between Washington and Tehran that began in late February.

item.title: White House calls leaked Iran draft deal a 'fabrication'
item.description: Iranian state television reported on Wednesday that it had obtained a draft of an "initial, unofficial" framework for a memorandum of understanding between the United States and Iran that would restore commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz to pre-war levels within one month of finalization. The White House quickly pushed back, calling the Iranian report a "total fabrication".

item.title: Oil supertankers cross Hormuz as strait traffic inches up
item.description:
Commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz showed faint signs of life this week as a COSCO oil products tanker navigated the waterway on Wednesday, a day after two non-Iranian crude supertankers made the crossing — the first time in a week that roughly four million barrels of unsanctioned crude were seen transiting the chokepoint.

The Singapore-linked Eagle Veracruz and Greek-owned Nissos Keros were both observed crossing Hormuz early on Tuesday, carrying crude from Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates respectively, according to vessel-tracking data reported by Bloomberg. Overall, five vessels traversed Hormuz in both directions on Tuesday, Bloomberg reported.

item.title: EU sets June 16 date to open Ukraine accession talks
item.description: The European Commission is preparing to propose the formal opening of the first cluster of EU membership negotiations with Ukraine and Moldova on June 16, with EU leaders expected to endorse the move at their summit on June 18-19, according to the Kyiv Post. The development comes after nearly two years of deadlock caused by Hungary's veto under former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán.

item.title: Israel declares 2,000 sq km of southern Lebanon a combat zone
item.description: Israel's military declared all areas south of the Zahrani River — roughly 2,000 square kilometers of southern Lebanon — a combat zone on Wednesday, warning residents to evacuate northward as it prepares for expanded operations against Hezbollah.

item.title: U.S. launches new airstrikes in southern Iran amid stalled ceasefire talks
item.description:
The U.S. military carried out new airstrikes in southern Iran targeting a military site believed to pose a threat to American forces and commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a U.S. official confirmed on Wednesday. U.S. forces also intercepted and shot down multiple Iranian drones in the region, according to ABC News.

The strikes come as negotiations between Washington and Tehran over a potential peace deal remain unsettled. Speaking at a cabinet meeting Wednesday, President Donald Trump said Iran "wants very much to make a deal" but added, "We're not satisfied with it, but that we will be. Either that or we'll have to just finish the job".

item.title: Iran's IRGC says it struck US airbase near Bandar Abbas
item.description:
The United States and Iran exchanged fresh military strikes on Thursday near the Strait of Hormuz, the most serious escalation since a ceasefire took effect on April 8, rattling energy markets and casting doubt over negotiations to end the conflict.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it targeted a US airbase early Thursday from which American forces had launched strikes on southern Iran near Bandar Abbas airport, according to Reuters and the Tasnim news agency. The IRGC described the attack as "a serious warning" to the United States. US Central Command had previously carried out what it termed "self-defense strikes" targeting missile launch sites and Iranian vessels attempting to lay mines near the strait.

item.title: Israel strikes Beirut suburb targeting Iranian militia missile commander
item.description:
Israel's air force carried out a targeted strike on the Choueifat area on the outskirts of Beirut's southern suburbs on Thursday afternoon, the first such attack near the Lebanese capital in weeks, as the military said it was targeting the head of the missile unit in the Imam Hussein Division, an Iran-linked militia operating alongside Hezbollah.

The target was identified as Ali al-Husseini, described by Israeli Army Radio as the commander of the rocket system within the Imam Hussein Division. It was not immediately clear whether al-Husseini was killed in the strike. The attack hit a building in Choueifat, with at least one person reported killed and several wounded, according to Lebanese media reports.

item.title: US and Iran reportedly reach 60-day MOU deal awaiting Trump's approval
item.description:
Negotiators from the United States and Iran have reached an agreement on a 60-day memorandum of understanding to extend their ceasefire and begin negotiations over Iran's nuclear program, but President Donald Trump still needs to give final approval, Axios reported on Thursday, citing two U.S. officials.

The reported breakthrough came on a day of renewed violence. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it struck a U.S. airbase early Thursday in retaliation for American strikes near the port city of Bandar Abbas, where U.S. forces had intercepted four Iranian attack drones and hit a ground-control station threatening commercial shipping near the Strait of Hormuz.
